name: delegate
description: Hand a self-contained job to a nested read-only agent and read its report right here. Use it to keep a wide search out of this conversation. The report comes back as the result of this call, in this same turn.

instructions.description: Everything the nested agent needs to do the job and report back. It shares this working directory but sees none of this conversation.

name: routine_list
description: Read every routine of this conversation, whichever agent here owns it. Read this before creating one, so you update what already covers the need instead of adding beside it.

name: routine_trigger_sources
description: Read what can fire a routine here and, for each source, the fields its events carry. Read this before creating or filtering a routine.

name: routine_create
description: Create a routine of this conversation, owned by you. Confirm the schedule and the task with the person, in their own words, before calling this.

title.description: A short name the person will recognise in the Routines panel.

instruction.description: What you carry out when this routine fires, written as an order to yourself.

triggerConfig.description: What the chosen source needs to fire, such as { expression: '0 8 * * 1-5' } for schedule.

triggerSourceId.description: The id of a source routine_trigger_sources answers, never one you invented.

filter.description: Which events run this routine. Leave it out to run on every event of the source.

name: routine_update
description: Rewrite a routine of this conversation, every field at once. Read it with routine_list first and send back what you are not changing.

title.description: A short name the person will recognise in the Routines panel.

instruction.description: What you carry out when this routine fires, written as an order to yourself.

triggerConfig.description: What the chosen source needs to fire, such as { expression: '0 8 * * 1-5' } for schedule.

id.description: The id of a routine routine_list answers.

filter.description: Which events run this routine. Leave it out to run on every event of the source.

isEnabled.description: Whether the routine fires. Turn it off instead of deleting it.

name: routine_run_now
description: Run a routine once, right now, without waiting for its trigger. Its report lands in this conversation like any other run.

id.description: The id of a routine routine_list answers.

name: routine_delete
description: Delete a routine and its run history. Ask the person first, and offer to turn it off instead when they only want it to stop for now.

id.description: The id of a routine routine_list answers.

name: mission_open
description: Open a mission on this conversation, owned by you, and get its own thread with one line telling whether that mission hears its coding session. Given the checkout the work happens in, the hook of the coding session is armed there in the same call. The work of the mission carries on in the thread it answers, so end the turn you are answering in with a single line of acknowledgement and nothing more. Call this once you and the person agree on the objective and the ticket it carries.

objective.description: What this mission delivers, in one sentence, written as an order to yourself.

platform.description: Where the ticket holding this objective lives.

externalId.description: The id the ticket carries on its own platform.

url.description: The address the person opens to read the ticket.

title.description: The title the ticket carries on its own platform.

tools.description: What this mission is allowed to reach for to meet its objective.

workspacePath.description: The git checkout on this computer the work of the mission happens in, a linked worktree included. Only a git checkout is accepted, so the path names a directory holding a .git entry and nothing else is taken. A path given arms the hook of the coding session in that checkout, so what a coding session does there reaches the thread of the mission. Left out, the mission moves only on the lines, the escalations and the closing you write.

name: mission_note
description: Record one line of progress on a mission of yours. Write what moved, not what you are about to do.

id.description: The id of the mission this lands on.

line.description: One line of progress, written for the person who reads the thread.

name: mission_status
description: Write the status of a mission of yours, every time you stop working on it, whether the work is over or only paused. It is a line for the reader and sets no state: whether the mission is idle, working or needs the person is observed by the host, never written by you. It is read by whoever follows the conversation the mission came from, who saw none of the work, so it holds on its own and names whoever moves next.

id.description: The id of the mission this lands on.

text.description: Where the mission stands, what moved since the last status, what is waiting and on whom, in a few plain lines.

name: mission_escalate
description: Hand a mission back to the person with the one question that blocks you. The mission waits until they answer.

id.description: The id of the mission this lands on.

question.description: The one question the person has to answer for you to carry on.

reason.description: Why you cannot decide it yourself.

name: mission_close
description: Close a mission of yours, its objective reached or given up, with a summary of where it landed. Nothing can be appended to it afterwards.

id.description: The id of the mission this lands on.

outcome.description: done when the objective is reached, failed when it is given up.

summary.description: What came out of the mission, in a few lines.

name: mission_watch
description: Arm a mission of yours on the branch it lands its work in, so what happens on that branch reaches its thread. It answers the address a call reaches the mission at, the key that call carries and the name of the header that key goes in. Call this once the branch exists.

id.description: The id of the mission this lands on.

branch.description: The branch this mission lands its work in, such as feature/ope-37.

repository.description: The repository that branch lives in, written owner then slash then name.

name: mission_list
description: Read the missions of this conversation, of every agent, open and closed, newest opened first, at most 200. Each comes with its id, its ticket, where it stands, the agent carrying it, the conversation it came from, its own thread, when it opened and closed, and its last status. Given a conversation, read that one instead. Given the space, read every mission of the space. Read this when you no longer hold the id of a mission, or to see what the others carry.

conversation.description: The id of a conversation of this space to read the missions of. Left out, this conversation.

space.description: true to read every mission of the space, whatever the conversation.

state.description: Keep only the missions standing there.

bot.description: The id of an agent, to keep only the missions it carries.

name: mission_read
description: Read one mission of this space, whoever carries it: its objective, its ticket, where it stands, the agent carrying it, the conversation it came from, its own thread, the branch and the repository it watches, its pull request, when it opened and closed, its last status, and every line written on it in order.

id.description: The id of the mission to read.

name: mission_reopen
description: Reopen a mission of yours that closed, done or failed, so its work carries on in the same thread and whatever watched it watches it again. A mission whose work was merged stays closed.

id.description: The id of the mission this lands on.

name: mission_update
description: Rewrite the objective, the ticket or the tools of a mission of yours when the person corrects them. Give only what changes, the rest stays as it is. A new objective also becomes the title of the thread of the mission.

id.description: The id of the mission this lands on.

objective.description: What this mission delivers, in one sentence, written as an order to yourself.

platform.description: Where the ticket holding this objective lives.

externalId.description: The id the ticket carries on its own platform.

url.description: The address the person opens to read the ticket.

title.description: The title the ticket carries on its own platform.

tools.description: What this mission is allowed to reach for to meet its objective.

name: mission_handoff
description: Hand a mission of yours over to another agent of this space, who owns it from then on. That agent is seated in the thread of the mission and in the conversation it came from, and is called in the thread while the mission is still open. You write nothing more on that mission afterwards.

id.description: The id of the mission this lands on.

companion.description: The name or the id of the agent of this space who takes the mission over.

name: application_search
description: Find the applications matching what the person asked for, the curated ones first, before you install any of them.

query.description: The words the person used for the application, its name or what it should do.

name: application_install
description: Install one application answered by application_search in the one destination the person picked, once they have picked it.

application.description: The exact name application_search answered for the application.

scope.description: The destination the person picked: companion (you alone), space or user.

name: application_status
description: Read where an application stands in one destination, when the person asks whether it is installed or connected.

application.description: The exact name application_search answered for the application.

scope.description: The destination the person picked: companion (you alone), space or user.

name: companion_suggestions
description: Read the agents this app suggests, each with the name, the job, the description and the blurb it ships, before you ask the person which one they want.

name: companion_create
description: Create an agent in the space of this conversation, once the person has picked a suggestion or agreed on the name, the job and the description you read back to them.

name.description: The name the person will call this agent by, theirs or the one they picked.

job.description: What this agent is for, in a few words, read under its name on its roster line.

description.description: What this agent does and how it works, written as an order to it.

name: companion_first_run_done
description: Record the first run of the app as finished, once the person has answered the hand-off question, so the app stops opening on it.

name: companion_list
description: List every agent of the space of this conversation, each with its id, its name and its job, before you seat one, take one out or mention one by name.

name: conversation_open
description: Open a new room in the space of this conversation, led by you, once the person asks for a topic of its own.

title.description: The title of the room, read in the space's list of rooms.

icon.description: The name of a Keyline icon drawn beside the title of the room, chosen with the title for the subject it names, such as Rocket, spelled as listed in packages/shared/conversation-icons.json. A name off that list is refused with the accepted names.

with.description: The id or the name of each agent of this space to seat in the room beside you, empty for you alone.

message.description: What you say to open the room, the first words read in it.

name: conversation_say
description: Say something in a room you hold a seat in, before you report back here on what you told it.

conversation.description: The id of the room you hold a seat in to say it in.

message.description: What you say in that room, read there in your name.

name: conversation_attach
description: Store any file for your message, in this conversation or in a room you hold a seat in, once you want the person to see it rather than only read it yourself, 10 MB per file: a file you show sits inside your message as the markdown line this answers, written exactly as answered where your reply cites the file, an image shown inline there and every other file as a link they open; the answer is the stored path, the id of that conversation and that markdown line, a line no reply of yours carries is added at the end of your last reply, and in a room the line is posted there for you.

path.description: The path of the file to show, absolute or relative to your working directory: any file up to 10 MB.

caption.description: The label of the markdown line, read as the alt text of an image or the text of a link, the name of the attached file when left out.

conversation.description: The id of a room you hold a seat in to show it there, left out for this conversation.

name: conversation_update
description: Change a conversation you hold a seat in, its title, its icon, its colour and who is seated in it, or reopen it once archived, every field given landing together in one call and none of them if one is refused, once the person asks for it or once its subject calls for it; the answer is the conversation as it stands after the call, with its id, kind, title, icon, colour, seated agents, last message and whether it is archived.

conversation.description: The id of the conversation to change, one you hold a seat in, left out for this conversation.

title.description: The new title of the conversation, the subject in a few words, left out to keep the one it wears; a title blank once trimmed is refused.

icon.description: The name of the Keyline icon drawn beside the title of the conversation, chosen for the subject the title names, left out to keep the one it wears. It is one of MessageSquare, Bug, Rocket, ShieldKey, Pen, FileText, Download, Laptop, Smartphone, BookOpen, CreditCard, Megaphone, PanelLeft, Code, Terminal, Server, Globe, Palette, Lightbulb, ChartLine, Calendar, Users, Flag, Sparkles, spelled exactly so; any other name is refused with the accepted names.

colour.description: A hue, a whole number from 0 to 359 around the colour wheel, or one of red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple or pink for the hue that name stands for, null to give the conversation back its default colour, left out to keep the one it wears; a hue outside 0 to 359 or another name is refused.

add.description: The id or the name of each agent of the space of the conversation to seat in it, recorded as invited by you; one already seated stays as it is, and a name two agents share is refused with their ids.

remove.description: The id or the name of each agent of the space of the conversation to take out of it, your own to leave it yourself; one not seated stays out.

archived.description: False to reopen an archived conversation, back in the list of rooms of the space with every message it held; true is refused, since only conversation_close archives a room; left out, the conversation stays archived or not as it is.

name: conversation_list
description: List the conversations of this space, the latest activity first, each with its id, its kind, its title, its icon, its colour, its agents, its last message and whether it is archived, before you read, join or mention one whose id you do not hold.

everywhere.description: True to list every conversation of this space, seated or not, false to list only the ones you hold a seat in; left out, it is false.

kind.description: One of main, topic or mission to list only that kind: main is an agent's own chat with the person, topic a room, mission the thread of a mission; left out, every kind is listed.

limit.description: How many conversations to answer, from 1 to 200; left out, 50.

cursor.description: The cursor the previous conversation_list answered, to list the page after it; left out, the list starts at the latest activity, and a null cursor in the answer marks the last page.

name: conversation_read
description: Read a conversation of this space, its details and its last messages oldest to newest, each with its seq, its author, its time and its full text, before you answer about what was said there, whether you hold a seat in it or not.

conversation.description: The id of the conversation of this space to read, as conversation_list answers it.

limit.description: How many messages to answer, from 1 to 100; left out, 20.

before.description: The cursor the previous conversation_read answered, to read the messages strictly older than the ones it answered; left out, the latest messages are read, and a null cursor in the answer marks the first message of the conversation.

name: conversation_search
description: Find where something was discussed in the space of this conversation, before you answer from memory or ask the person where it was said: it answers conversations, the rooms whose title or agent names match, each with its id, its kind (main, topic or mission), its title (the agent's name for a main conversation) and the names of the agents seated in it, and messages, the messages whose text matches, best match first, each with the conversationId and conversationTitle of its room, its messageId, its author (the id of the agent who wrote it, or null when the person did), its createdAt in milliseconds since the epoch and a snippet of plain text around the match; two empty lists mean nothing in this space matched, and no other space is ever searched.

query.description: The words to look for, matched against the start of words in messages and inside room titles and agent names, at most 200 characters.

kind.description: One of main (an agent's own conversation with the person), topic (a room) or mission, to keep only the conversations and the messages of that kind, left out for every kind.

name: conversation_close
description: Archive a room you lead once its subject is settled, keeping every message in it.

conversation.description: The id of the room you lead to archive.

name: bundle_write
description: Write one file of your own directory, the one your instructions name as the place your skills live, and keep it as one change in your history. A skill file under skills/ ending in .md is written whole, its folders created. For agents/agent.md the text is the whole block of what you learned: the block is created on your first write when the file has none, and the rest of the file is kept as the app renders it. It answers the id of the change, or unchanged when the file already says that.

path.description: The file, relative to your own directory: skills/<name>/SKILL.md, another .md under skills/, or agents/agent.md.

text.description: The whole new text of a skill file, or for agents/agent.md the whole new text of the block of what you learned, without its two kiroshi lines.

title.description: What changed, in one line of at most 72 characters, in the language of the conversation, for someone who does not read code.

summary.description: One to three lines saying what changed and why, in the language of the conversation.

name: get_guide
description: The guide to working in the Library of this Space: boards for its boards, documents for the Library and its Markdown documents. Call it once per session with the matching topic, before the first library_, document_, board_ or screenshot call. It answers the guide as Markdown.

topic.description: boards for a board, documents for the Library and its documents.

name: library_list
description: List the items of the Library of this Space, the latest update first, each with its name, its kind (document, image or board) and its updatedAt in milliseconds since the epoch, before you read, write, rename or delete one whose name you do not hold.

kind.description: One of document, image or board to list only that kind; left out, every kind is listed.

limit.description: How many items to answer, from 1 to 200; left out, 50.

cursor.description: The cursor the previous library_list answered, to list the page after it; left out, the list starts at the latest update, and a null cursor in the answer marks the last page.

name: library_search
description: Find the items of the Library of this Space whose name, document text or board text holds the words you give, whatever their case, each with its name, its kind and its updatedAt, the latest update first; an empty list means nothing in this Library matched, and no other Space is ever searched.

query.description: The words to look for, matched whatever their case.

name: library_read
description: Read an item of the Library of this Space by its name. A document answers its text as it stands now with what everyone has typed in it; to change a Markdown document, read its blocks with document_tree instead. A board answers its JSON Canvas text; an image is shown to you; an image too large to show answers its name, its type and its size.

name.description: The name of the item in the Library of this Space, with its extension, such as notes.md.

name: library_create
description: Create a new Markdown document in the Library of this Space, empty or filled from a template, shown in the Library of the person right away. A name already taken is refused. To change a document that already exists, edit its blocks with document_tree then document_replace_block or document_insert_after, never create another one. It answers the name the document stands under, its kind and its updatedAt.

name.description: The name of the new document, ending in .md, such as minutes.md, without any folder.

template.description: One of meeting-notes, project-brief, decision-record or weekly-update to start the document from that template; left out, the document starts empty.

name: library_import
description: Copy a file you produced into the Library of this Space, a Markdown or text document, a JSON Canvas board ending in .canvas or a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image. Left without overwrite, it lands under its own name, a number added when that name is taken. Changing an item that already exists, such as an image you imported before, means naming it in overwrite so the file replaces it in place, never adding a new one. It answers the name the item stands under, its kind and its updatedAt.

path.description: The path of the file to copy, absolute or relative to your working directory.

overwrite.description: The name of an item of this Library the file replaces in place, such as chart.png: a document for a document, an image of the same format for an image; a board is never replaced. A name absent from this Library or of another kind is refused and nothing changes. Leave it out to add a new item.

name: library_rename
description: Rename a document of the Library of this Space, keeping its extension, as the person renames it: the people editing it follow it under the new name, a number added when that name is taken. It answers the name it landed under, its kind and its updatedAt.

name.description: The name of the item in the Library of this Space, with its extension, such as notes.md.

newName.description: The new name of the document, with the same extension, without any folder.

name: library_delete
description: Delete an item of the Library of this Space for everyone, with its thumbnail and its shared editing state, once the person asked you to remove it. It can't be undone. It answers the name of the item deleted.

name.description: The name of the item in the Library of this Space, with its extension, such as notes.md.

name: conversation_post_document
description: Post a document or a board of the Library of this Space in this conversation, as a message of yours the person opens it from, once you want them to read it. A name that is not a document or a board of this Library is refused and nothing is posted. It answers the name of the item, the id of this conversation and the id of the message.

name.description: The name of the item in the Library of this Space, with its extension, such as notes.md.

name: document_info
description: Describe a Markdown document of the Library of this Space in one short answer: its name, its updatedAt in milliseconds since the epoch, how many blocks it holds and the id of its first heading, null when it has none. Call it first to size a document before you read its tree.

name.description: The name of a Markdown document of the Library of this Space, such as notes.md.

name: document_tree
description: List the blocks of a Markdown document of the Library of this Space in order, as they stand now with what everyone has typed in it. Each block answers its id, its kind (heading, paragraph, list, checklist, quote, code, table, rule or image), its level for a heading, and its first words. Read the tree before you change a document: every other document tool targets a block by its id.

name.description: The name of a Markdown document of the Library of this Space, such as notes.md.

name: document_read_block
description: Read one block of a Markdown document of the Library of this Space by its id, as document_tree answered it. It answers the kind of the block and its Markdown.

name.description: The name of a Markdown document of the Library of this Space, such as notes.md.

id.description: The id of a block of the document, as document_tree answered it. An id absent from the document is refused and nothing changes.

name: document_insert_after
description: Write new blocks into a Markdown document of the Library of this Space, live, beside the people editing it, right after the block named in after, or at the start of the document when after is left out. To add at the end, name the id of the last block of document_tree. It answers the ids of the new blocks, in order.

name.description: The name of a Markdown document of the Library of this Space, such as notes.md.

after.description: The id of the block the new blocks land right after, as document_tree answered it; left out, they land at the start of the document.

markdown.description: The Markdown of one or more blocks, such as a heading, paragraphs, a list or a table, blocks apart by a blank line. Write no block id: each new block gets its own.

name: document_replace_block
description: Replace one block of a Markdown document of the Library of this Space with new Markdown, live, beside the people editing it: a new title, a rewritten paragraph or list. The first new block keeps the id of the block it replaces. Changing a document that already exists means editing it here in place, never creating a new one. It answers the id of every resulting block, in order.

name.description: The name of a Markdown document of the Library of this Space, such as notes.md.

id.description: The id of a block of the document, as document_tree answered it. An id absent from the document is refused and nothing changes.

markdown.description: The Markdown of one or more blocks, such as a heading, paragraphs, a list or a table, blocks apart by a blank line. Write no block id: each new block gets its own.

name: document_delete_block
description: Remove blocks of a Markdown document of the Library of this Space by their ids, live, beside the people editing it. One id absent from the document refuses the whole call and nothing changes. It answers the ids removed.

name.description: The name of a Markdown document of the Library of this Space, such as notes.md.

ids.description: The ids of the blocks to remove, as document_tree answered them.

name: document_find
description: Find the blocks of a Markdown document of the Library of this Space holding the text you give, whatever its case. It answers each matching block with its id, its kind and the first line of it that holds the text.

name.description: The name of a Markdown document of the Library of this Space, such as notes.md.

text.description: The text to look for, matched whatever its case.

name: board_create
description: Create a new empty board in the Library of this Space, shown in the Library of the person right away. A name already taken is refused and nothing is created. To draw on a board that already exists, write into it with board_write, never create another one. It answers the name the board stands under, its kind and its updatedAt. Every answer also carries a header: the name of the board, its updatedAt and a hash of its content that changes whenever a node or an arrow changes and stays equal otherwise, so a hash other than the one you hold means someone drew on the board since.

name.description: The name of the board in the Library of this Space, ending in .canvas, such as roadmap.canvas, without any folder.

name: board_info
description: Orient on a board of the Library of this Space before reading it in detail, whoever drew on it. It answers how many nodes of each kind it holds, how many arrows, the bounds of all its nodes, and the id, label, x, y, width and height of every section at its top level. Every answer also carries a header: the name of the board, its updatedAt and a hash of its content that changes whenever a node or an arrow changes and stays equal otherwise, so a hash other than the one you hold means someone drew on the board since.

name.description: The name of the board in the Library of this Space, ending in .canvas, such as roadmap.canvas, without any folder.

name: board_tree
description: List the nodes of a board of the Library of this Space under a parent, the board itself or one of its sections, as they stand now with what everyone has drawn. Each node answers its id, its kind, an excerpt of its text of 60 characters at most (the label of a section, the file of an image or a libraryCard, the title or the url of a linkCard), its x, y, width and height, its z-order and its parent, the smallest section whose rectangle holds it. Given a depth, it stops that many levels down and answers for each node at that limit the count of its children it left out. It also lists every arrow whose two ends lie under that parent, with its id, its fromNode or fromPoint, its toNode or toPoint and its label. A parent absent from the board, or that is not a section, is refused with its id. Every answer also carries a header: the name of the board, its updatedAt and a hash of its content that changes whenever a node or an arrow changes and stays equal otherwise, so a hash other than the one you hold means someone drew on the board since.

name.description: The name of the board in the Library of this Space, ending in .canvas, such as roadmap.canvas, without any folder.

parent.description: The id of a section of the board, as board_tree answered it; left out, the board itself.

depth.description: How many levels under the parent to list, 1 for its children alone; left out, every level.

name: board_node_info
description: Read every JSON Canvas field of nodes and arrows of a board of the Library of this Space by id. A node answers its kind, x, y, width, height, z-order, text or label, color, fill, shape and any other field it carries, such as the file of an image: call board_view with its id to see an image. An arrow answers its fromNode or fromPoint, fromSide, fromAnchor, fromEnd, toNode or toPoint, toSide, toAnchor, toEnd, color, label, labelPosition, bend, routing and headSize. A field never set answers its default, or null. An id absent from the board refuses the whole call with that id. Every answer also carries a header: the name of the board, its updatedAt and a hash of its content that changes whenever a node or an arrow changes and stays equal otherwise, so a hash other than the one you hold means someone drew on the board since.

name.description: The name of the board in the Library of this Space, ending in .canvas, such as roadmap.canvas, without any folder.

nodes.description: The ids of the nodes to read, as board_tree answered them.

arrows.description: The ids of the arrows to read, as board_tree answered them.

name: board_canvas
description: Read the JSON Canvas text of a board of the Library of this Space, or of one of its sections with every node the section holds and the arrows between them. Every answer also carries a header: the name of the board, its updatedAt and a hash of its content that changes whenever a node or an arrow changes and stays equal otherwise, so a hash other than the one you hold means someone drew on the board since.

name.description: The name of the board in the Library of this Space, ending in .canvas, such as roadmap.canvas, without any folder.

parent.description: The id of a section of the board, as board_tree answered it; left out, the board itself.

name: board_write
description: Write one group of nodes and arrows into a parent of a board of the Library of this Space, the board itself or one of its sections, landing at once for the people who have it open. Give every node a key of your own; place it at x and y, beside another node with place, or inside a section with section, and the board computes where it lands without covering another node. A node with no section lands inside the parent, which grows to hold it. An arrow names its ends with fromNode and toNode, each the key of a node of this call or the id of a node of the board, or leaves an end free at fromPoint or toPoint. An arrow without routing is an elbow tied on the sides of its two nodes that face each other. In replace mode, the nodes the parent section holds and every arrow tied to them are removed in the same change, the section itself kept; replace without a parent is refused as missingParent and nothing changes. An id absent from the board, or one invalid node or arrow, refuses the whole call with its element, its index and the reason, and nothing changes. It answers the id each key got. Every answer also carries a header: the name of the board, its updatedAt and a hash of its content that changes whenever a node or an arrow changes and stays equal otherwise, so a hash other than the one you hold means someone drew on the board since.

name.description: The name of the board in the Library of this Space, ending in .canvas, such as roadmap.canvas, without any folder.

parent.description: The id of a section of the board, as board_tree answered it; left out, the board itself.

mode.description: insert to add the group beside what the parent holds, replace to remove what the parent section holds first; replace needs a parent.

nodes.description: The nodes to write, in order: each node without a place lands right of the one before it, inside the parent.

key.description: A name of your own for this node, unique in this call, that the place, the section and the arrows of this call use to point at it.

kind.description: One of sticky, text, shape or section.

text.description: The text the node shows; for a section, its label.

color.description: A colour, a preset from 1 to 6 or a hex such as #4a90d9.

fill.description: For a sticky only, one of yellow, green, pink, blue or orange.

shape.description: For a shape only, one of rectangle, ellipse or diamond.

x.description: An exact board coordinate, given with its pair; left out, the board places the node.

y.description: An exact board coordinate, given with its pair; left out, the board places the node.

width.description: In board units; left out, the default size of the kind.

height.description: In board units; left out, the default size of the kind.

place.description: Where the node lands next to another one, at a fixed gap and centred on it.

side.description: One of right, left, below or above.

of.description: The key of a node of this call or the id of a node of the board the node lands beside.

section.description: The key of a section of this call or the id of a section of the board the node lands inside; the section grows to hold it. Left out, the parent.

arrows.description: The arrows to write between the nodes.

key.description: A name of your own for this arrow, unique in this call, to find its id in the answer.

fromNode.description: The node this end ties to: the key of a node of this call or the id of a node of the board.

fromSide.description: One of top, right, bottom or left: the side of the node this end ties to; never with an anchor.

fromAnchor.description: The exact point of the node this end ties to, x and y from 0 to 1 across it; never with a side.

fromPoint.description: A free end at a board x and y, tied to no node.

fromEnd.description: One of none or arrow: whether this end draws an arrowhead.

toNode.description: The node this end ties to: the key of a node of this call or the id of a node of the board.

toSide.description: One of top, right, bottom or left: the side of the node this end ties to; never with an anchor.

label.description: The text written on the arrow.

labelPosition.description: Where the label sits along the arrow, from 0 at its start to 1 at its end, 0.5 by default.

bend.description: How far the arrow bows, in board units, 0 for none.

routing.description: One of straight or elbow; left out on a new arrow, elbow.

headSize.description: One of small, medium or large.

name: board_update
description: Change fields of nodes and of arrows of a board of the Library of this Space by id, drawn by you or by a person, every field a patch does not name kept as it stands, in one change the people who have it open see at once. x, y, width and height move and resize a node of any kind, an image and a libraryCard included; text, color, fill and shape apply only to a kind that carries them. Tying an end of an arrow to a node frees its point and the reverse; a side replaces an anchor and the reverse. An id absent from the board, or a field the node or the arrow refuses, refuses the whole call with its element, its index and the reason, and nothing changes. It answers the ids of the nodes and of the arrows changed. Every answer also carries a header: the name of the board, its updatedAt and a hash of its content that changes whenever a node or an arrow changes and stays equal otherwise, so a hash other than the one you hold means someone drew on the board since.

name: board_move
description: Move nodes of a board of the Library of this Space into a parent, the board itself or one of its sections, the top left of their bounds landing at x and y. Every node keeps its id and every arrow stays tied to it; a moved section carries every node it holds by the same offset, and the target section grows to hold what lands in it. An id absent from the board, or a section moved into itself, refuses the whole call and nothing changes. It answers the ids of the nodes moved. Every answer also carries a header: the name of the board, its updatedAt and a hash of its content that changes whenever a node or an arrow changes and stays equal otherwise, so a hash other than the one you hold means someone drew on the board since.

name: board_duplicate
description: Copy nodes of a board of the Library of this Space, with every node a copied section holds and every arrow whose two ends are copied, right of the originals clear of the other nodes, or with the top left of their bounds at x and y. An id absent from the board refuses the whole call and nothing changes. It answers each old node id and each old arrow id with the id of its copy. Every answer also carries a header: the name of the board, its updatedAt and a hash of its content that changes whenever a node or an arrow changes and stays equal otherwise, so a hash other than the one you hold means someone drew on the board since.

name: board_delete
description: Remove nodes and arrows of any kind from a board of the Library of this Space by id, drawn by you or by a person, a section with every node it holds and every arrow tied to a removed node, in one change. An id absent from the board refuses the whole call with that id and nothing changes. It answers the ids of the nodes and of the arrows removed. Every answer also carries a header: the name of the board, its updatedAt and a hash of its content that changes whenever a node or an arrow changes and stays equal otherwise, so a hash other than the one you hold means someone drew on the board since.

name: board_find
description: Find the nodes of a board of the Library of this Space matching every criterion you give among the text they show, whatever its case, their kind, color, fill and shape. It answers their ids, lowest z-order first; given no criterion, every node. Every answer also carries a header: the name of the board, its updatedAt and a hash of its content that changes whenever a node or an arrow changes and stays equal otherwise, so a hash other than the one you hold means someone drew on the board since.

name: board_view
description: Show you an image node of a board of the Library of this Space as an image, whoever dropped it there. A node that is not an image, an image whose file is not in the Library of this Space, or an image too large to show is refused with the node id and the reason, the size and the limit for one too large, and nothing is shown. Every answer also carries a header: the name of the board, its updatedAt and a hash of its content that changes whenever a node or an arrow changes and stays equal otherwise, so a hash other than the one you hold means someone drew on the board since.

id.description: The id of an image node of the board, as board_tree answered it.

name: screenshot
description: Show you a picture of a board or of a Markdown document of the Library of this Space as a person sees it there, in the light theme, rendered from what is saved at the moment of the call. Call it after a write to check what you drew or wrote. A board name alone shows every node and arrow of the board, framed on their bounds; with the id of a node, that node and the nodes it holds. A document name alone shows the whole document; with the id of a block, that block alone. An id absent from the board or the document is refused with that id, and a board or a document with nothing in it as nothingToShow, before anything is rendered; a render that does not answer within 15 seconds is refused as renderTimedOut. It answers the picture, at most 1568 pixels on its long edge, with the header of board_info for a board or the answer of document_info for a document, and the rendered width, height and scale.

name.description: The name of a board ending in .canvas, such as roadmap.canvas, or of a Markdown document, such as notes.md, of the Library of this Space, without any folder.

id.description: The id of a node of the board as board_tree answered it, or of a block of the document as document_tree answered it. Left out, the whole board or document.

scale.description: 1 or 2: the pixels drawn for each point of the board or the document. Left out, 1.

name: comment_list
description: List the comment threads people and agents opened on an item of the Library of this Space, a document, an image or a board, in the order they were opened. Each thread answers its threadId, its state (open or resolved), its target (a block or a passage of a document, a point or a zone of an image, a node or a point of a board), whether that target is gone from the item, how many comments it holds and the first words of its opening comment. An item nobody commented answers an empty list.

name.description: The name of the item in the Library of this Space, with its extension, such as notes.md.

name: comment_read
description: Read one comment thread of an item of the Library of this Space by its threadId, as comment_list answered it. It answers the name and the kind of the item, the state of the thread, its target with the text of the block it points at for a document, and every comment in order with its author, its text and the people and agents it mentions.

name.description: The name of the item in the Library of this Space, with its extension, such as notes.md.

threadId.description: The id of a comment thread of the item, as comment_list answered it.

name: comment_reply
description: Reply in a comment thread of an item of the Library of this Space, as a comment of yours the people of the Space read under your name beside the item. Reply once the work the thread asks for is done, or to say why it is not. A threadId absent from the item, or a blank text, is refused and nothing is written. It answers the threadId and how many comments the thread holds now.

name.description: The name of the item in the Library of this Space, with its extension, such as notes.md.

threadId.description: The id of a comment thread of the item, as comment_list answered it.

text.description: The text of your comment, in plain words.
